name: Contrast: although, despite, however
subtitle: Show a surprising contrast with although / even though + clause, despite / in spite of + noun or -ing, or however between two sentences: Although it was cold, we went out. Despite the cold, we went out.

concept.exampleHtml: Although it was cold, we went out. · Despite the cold, we went out. · It was cold. However, we went out.

qa.html: A contrast joins two facts when the second one is surprising. At A2 you know but: It was cold, but we went out. At B1 you also use although, despite and however. They give you more ways to say the same thing.

although / even though + subject + verb. Even though is a little stronger. The clause can come first (then use a comma) or second (no comma): Although it was cold, we went out. We went out although it was cold. Don't add but.
despite / in spite of + a noun or an -ing form, not a clause: Despite the cold, we went out. In spite of being tired, she went to work. The two words mean the same. Never say despite of.
however starts a new sentence. Put a full stop before it and a comma after it: It was cold. However, we went out. It does not join two clauses like but does.

Typical mistakes: ✗ Although it was cold, but we went out. → ✓ Although it was cold, we went out. (not both) · ✗ Despite it was cold, we went out. / Despite of the cold… → ✓ Despite the cold, we went out. · ✗ It was cold, however we went out. → ✓ It was cold. However, we went out.

concept.noteHtml: After despite you can use an -ing form, see Gerunds. If you want a clause after despite, say despite the fact that: Despite the fact that it was cold, we went out. (although is shorter). But is the simplest choice in everyday speech. Although, despite and however are common in writing and in longer answers.

listen.text: Although it was raining, we went for a walk.
listen.note: although + subject + verb. A comma follows the clause. No but.

listen.text: Despite the rain, we went for a walk.
listen.note: despite + noun. It is not followed by a clause.

listen.text: It was raining. However, we went for a walk.
listen.note: However starts a new sentence and is followed by a comma.

rounds.label: 1 · although
rounds.instruction: You hear a sentence with but. Say it again with although, and start with although.

example.prompt: It was cold, but we went out.
example.answer: Although it was cold, we went out.

items.prompt: He was tired, but he went to work.
items.answer: Although he was tired, he went to work.

items.prompt: It was expensive, but she bought it.
items.answer: Although it was expensive, she bought it.

items.prompt: I studied a lot, but I failed the test.
items.answer: Although I studied a lot, I failed the test.

items.prompt: The flat is small, but we like it.
items.answer: Although the flat is small, we like it.

items.prompt: It was raining, but the match started.
items.answer: Although it was raining, the match started.

items.prompt: She felt ill, but she went to the party.
items.answer: Although she felt ill, she went to the party.

rounds.label: 2 · despite + noun
rounds.instruction: You hear a sentence with although. Say it with despite and a noun.

example.prompt: Although the weather was bad, we went out.
example.answer: Despite the bad weather, we went out.

items.prompt: Although the traffic was heavy, he arrived on time.
items.answer: Despite the heavy traffic, he arrived on time.

items.prompt: Although the exam was difficult, she passed.
items.answer: Despite the difficult exam, she passed.

items.prompt: Although the rain was heavy, we played football.
items.answer: Despite the heavy rain, we played football.

items.prompt: Although the journey was long, they enjoyed it.
items.answer: Despite the long journey, they enjoyed it.

items.prompt: Although the price was high, I bought the coat.
items.answer: Despite the high price, I bought the coat.

items.prompt: Although the noise was loud, the baby slept.
items.answer: Despite the loud noise, the baby slept.

exercises.title: although, despite or however? Complete the sentences.
exercises.hint: Look at what follows the gap: a clause (subject + verb), a noun, or a comma and a new sentence.
exercises.hintHtml: althoughA clause follows: subject + verb.despiteA noun or an -ing form follows.howeverA new sentence, with a comma after it.

items.prompt: ___ it was raining, we went for a walk.
items.why: A clause follows (it was raining): although.

items.prompt: ___ the rain, we went for a walk.
It was raining. ___, we went for a walk.
items.why: A new sentence with a comma after the word: however.

items.prompt: She passed the exam ___ her illness.
___ he was tired, he finished the report.
items.why: A clause follows (he was tired): although.

items.prompt: The hotel was cheap. ___, it was very comfortable.
items.why: It starts a new sentence, with a comma after: However.

items.prompt: We enjoyed the trip ___ the long journey.
items.why: A noun follows (the long journey): despite.

items.prompt: He didn't call ___ he promised to.

exercises.title: The sentence pattern decides: complete with the right word.
exercises.hint: but joins two clauses with a comma. although starts a clause. despite is followed by a noun. however starts a new sentence.
exercises.hintHtml: butTwo clauses, a comma before but.althoughA clause follows: subject + verb.despiteA noun follows.howeverA new sentence, with a comma after.

items.prompt: It was cold, ___ we went out.
items.why: Two clauses with a comma between them: but.

items.prompt: ___ it was cold, we went out.
items.why: A clause follows and no but is needed: although.

items.prompt: It was cold. ___, we went out.
items.why: A new sentence starts here: However, with a comma.

items.prompt: ___ the cold, we went out.
I like the flat, ___ it's very small.
items.why: Both work. But joins two clauses. Although adds the surprising fact.

items.prompt: The train was late. ___, I got to work on time.
items.why: A new sentence starts here: However, with a comma.

items.prompt: She studied hard, ___ she failed the test.
items.why: Two clauses with a comma between them: but. However needs a full stop before it.

items.prompt: He went to work ___ his headache.
